chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the adhan, and he said:

You say: Allah is greater, Allah is greater. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. Come to salat (prayer), come to salat (prayer). Come to success, come to success. Come to the best of deeds, come to the best of deeds. Allah is greater, Allah is greater. There is no god but Allah, there is no god but Allah.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; the formula of testimony in the adhan
key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: Allah is greater; the takbir formula
key_terms.حَيَّ عَلَى خَيْرِ الْعَمَلِ: come to the best of deeds
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah; the prophetic testimony
key_terms.لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: there is no god but Allah; the declaration of tawhid

ai.seo_question: What is the wording of the adhan according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the wording and number of the phrases of the adhan as taught by Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام. It is significant in Shia jurisprudence for preserving the transmitted form of the call to prayer, including the phrase ḥayya 'ala khayr al-'amal.
